# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Re:** Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 20, 2026
**Governing Policy:** Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O) — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf
**Member:** Avery Alvarez
**Member ID:** W460125797
**Reference Number:** POC-55381BDBC3-44861
**Plan:** UnitedHealthcare Community Plan (Commercial/ACA), State of Hawaii

Dear UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which was denied on August 20, 2026, with the stated reason that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision because my medical records already contain the information needed to evaluate my case, and my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary.

## Why I believe my records support this surgery

The plan's own policy, Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O), states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

The policy directs reviewers to specific clinical criteria for this exact procedure:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

> "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

My total ankle replacement falls squarely under "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" in this list. However, the denial notice did not tell me which specific InterQual criteria were applied to my case or which part of my documentation was considered incomplete. My records include the following, which I believe are directly relevant to a medical-necessity review of ankle TJR:

- **12 months** of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest
- **10 weeks of supervised physical therapy** (16 visits, May 15, 2026 – July 24, 2026), documented in the physical therapy discharge note
- **6 months of NSAID use** with inadequate relief
- A **corticosteroid injection** on April 29, 2026, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief
- **Weight-bearing ankle radiographs (July 12, 2026)** showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts
- An **antalgic gait**, with walking limited to two blocks
- **Positive provocative testing** on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker

I have completed a documented course of conservative treatment — physical therapy, medication, and injection — without lasting relief, and imaging confirms significant joint damage. My surgeon has reviewed this history and has documented that surgery is needed.

The policy also states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand this documentation does not guarantee approval, but I believe the records above are the kind of documentation the plan's own policy contemplates, and I am asking that they be reviewed in full against the applicable InterQual criteria.

I want to note that the policy excerpts I received also include language about osteochondral allograft and autograft transplant for cartilage defects. That is a different procedure from the total ankle replacement my surgeon has requested, and I do not believe it applies to my case. If the plan applied that language to my denial, I would ask that this be clarified and corrected.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

UnitedHealthcare's policy states that the plan "may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits." Because InterQual is licensed software and not a public document, I am requesting — as is my right under federal appeal rules — that the plan provide, in writing and free of charge, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, along with a specific explanation of what documentation was considered missing or incomplete.

## What I am asking for

I am asking UnitedHealthcare Community Plan to:

1. Reconsider the denial of CPT 27702 (total ankle replacement) for Member ID W460125797, reference number POC-55381BDBC3-44861;
2. Provide the specific InterQual subset, edition, and criteria applied to my case, as requested above; and
3. Review the clinical documentation summarized in this letter, together with any additional records my surgeon submits, before making a final decision.

I understand my appeal must be received by **February 16, 2027**, though I understand the date on my denial letter is authoritative if it differs. I am submitting this appeal by signing in at member.uhc.com, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, and/or by mailing it to the address printed on my denial letter. [Insert specific mailing address from denial letter, if applicable]

Please contact me if any additional information is needed. I have asked Dr. Reyes's office to send supporting records directly as well.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Avery Alvarez
Member ID: W460125797
[Mailing address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of letter]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
